prompt: Bug report from a user: "My GPS app writes the `# units: ft` line at the end of the file, after the points. trailhead then reports a highest point of 14115 m for a hike that tops out at 14,115 ft (about 4302 m). The file is attached as `pikes-peak.csv`." Find the cause and fix it.
bash_commands: cat src/trailhead/track.py; cat pikes-peak.csv | head; tail -3 pikes-peak.csv

python - <<'EOF'
import re,pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("src/trailhead/track.py"); s=p.read_text()
s=s.replace("""        points.append(_parse_point(line, number, scale))
    if len(points) < 2:
        raise TrackError("a track needs at least two points")
    return Track(name, points)""","""        points.append(_parse_point(line, number))
    if len(points) < 2:
        raise TrackError("a track needs at least two points")
    # Settings apply to the whole track wherever they appear, so convert units only
    # after every line, including a trailing "# units:" line, has been read.
    if scale != 1.0:
        points = [Point(p.lat, p.lon, p.ele * scale) for p in points]
    return Track(name, points)""")
s=s.replace("def _parse_point(line: str, number: int, scale: float) -> Point:","def _parse_point(line: str, number: int) -> Point:")
s=s.replace("return Point(lat, lon, ele * scale)","return Point(lat, lon, ele)")
p.write_text(s)
EOF
grep -rn "_parse_point\|units" tests | head -20
python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; PYTHONPATH=src python -m trailhead summary pikes-peak.csv
